features.ip_note: Datacenter pool by default ($1.08/GB Discovery), residential pool $7.99/GB Discovery down to $6.05/GB Enterprise, plus managed Tor; no mobile or BYO proxy documented.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Very low prepaid effective hourly rate excludes bandwidth. Do not use fee/credits as overflow rate: published overage is higher.
Cloud Browser docs explicitly define GB=1024 MB, unlike default estimator GB≈GiB simplification. MB rounds up; VNC/RTC add-ons and CAPTCHA consume the same quota.

5-credit allocation minimum applies to combined time + traffic, not five extra credits on every session. It cannot be exactly represented by card start_fee. Card uses null rather than inventing a time-only minimum.
Credit overflow is purchased in 10 k blocks; engine continuous arithmetic needs ceiling correction. Discovery stops at quota. Free grant 1,000 credits once, not $1,000.
Session resume (auto_close=false) keeps the browser running and billing after disconnect; there is no free paused state.

Pay-as-you-go overflow is automatic on Pro+, but 'Some accounts require a balance to consume Pay As You Go usage' and are rejected with HTTP 429 when the prepaid balance does not cover it. Discovery/Pro/Startup are suspended immediately on failed payment (Enterprise 7-day, Custom 30-day grace).
Unused plan credits do not roll over.

Cloud Browser /unblock endpoint (anti-bot pre-bypassed session, residential only): the billing calculator applies UNBLOCK_SURCHARGE = 1.2 to the residential credits/MB rate (e.g. Pro 78 -> 94 credits/MB). Sessions 'are billed until explicitly closed or they reach the browser_timeout limit' (max 1800 s).

fleet.verification: No card for free key, but official KYC policy applies to ALL customers: company name/address/activity, phone, email, planned use/experience; automated identity checks and manual use-case review. Further information can be requested.
fleet.tiers: Discovery 5, Pro 20, Startup 50, Enterprise 100; Custom committed concurrency.
fleet.notes: New signup includes 1,000 free credits but inspected pricing does not state its concurrency; paid Discovery 5 is not presumed trial default. 10 Pro, 50 Startup, 300/1,000 Custom. Request concurrency not generic machines. KYC page says most signups activate in minutes; that is not a quota increase SLA.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: After a Cloud Browser run stops, its full profile (cookies, storage, tokens, fingerprint, proxy identity) is saved to storage.
snapshot_auto.note: Browser product. On a clean stop of a named session the browser profile (cookies, local/sessionStorage, trust tokens, fingerprint, proxy identity; no tabs or live JS state) is saved automatically, but it is documented only as a one-way handoff into the Web Scraping API (session=cb:<id>), not restored into a new Cloud Browser session. Session resume (auto_close=false) just keeps the live browser running and billing until timeout (max 30 min); after termination reconnect fails ('Session expired or was terminated'). So no automatic save/restore of the browser machine on the next start.

harness_api.quote: takes a plain-English task description, plans the scraping steps, executes them using Scrapfly tools, and returns structured results
harness_api.note: `scrapfly agent` is a client-side CLI agent loop using your own LLM key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY etc.) that calls browser tools; it does not run inside the cloud browser and there is no API to drive an agent harness inside the session. Browser Use / Stagehand / Vercel agent-browser integrations run on the customer's side and connect over CDP; the optional in-browser MCP endpoint (enable_mcp) exposes browser tools, not a harness.

ingress_rules.quote: Comma-separated list of IPs or CIDRs trusted to attach without a password.
ingress_rules.note: Applies to the live-control endpoints of a session (VNC/RTC human-in-the-loop): off unless enable_vnc etc. is set, attach requires a user-chosen session password, optional hitl_allowed_networks IP/CIDR list. CDP WebSocket requires the API key. There are no arbitrary exposed service ports in this product.

guest_firewall.note: Managed Chromium (Scrapium) sessions accessed only over CDP/WebSocket (plus optional VNC); no shell/root in the browser host, so no in-guest nftables/iptables. Not stated explicitly in docs; follows from the product model.

secret_proxy.quote: Your code passes a vault name and a key on the connection URL. It never sees the password itself.
secret_proxy.note: Related but different: the Credential Vault (rolling out gradually; optional 1Password mirror) autofills login passwords/TOTP into the browser's password store server-side and redacts them from screenshots, DOM, VNC and Runtime.evaluate results, so the controlling script/agent never sees them. It is form autofill inside the browser (the secret does enter the browser process), not a proxy injecting credentials into outbound HTTP requests; API-credential 'blob' items are never injected into the browser. No HTTP header/credential injection proxy documented.
